target_module: impl_top (the top module -- the Trojan sits directly on the RX-to-TX datapath assignment, which only exists at this level)
trigger_description: uart_rx_data (the single received-byte operand, with no AND/XOR combination against any other signal and no counter/timebomb) equals exactly 8'h93. P = 2^-8 per byte, never reached by golden testbench traffic (its full 58-distinct-byte stimulus set was enumerated in Python and confirmed to never include 0x93).
observable_effect: uart_tx_data is assigned uart_rx_data ^ 8'hFF instead of uart_rx_data, but ONLY for the single operand value 0x93; all 255 other byte values pass through the retransmit path bit-exact. This corrupts the retransmitted/echoed byte on uart_txd only -- the receiver's own internal state (uart_rx_data) and the led output (which is wired from uart_rx_data directly, not from the corrupted uart_tx_data) both continue to show the TRUE received byte 0x93 correctly. This is a textbook parametric rare-value corruption: a pure single-operand equality check with no latching, no state, no timing dependency, and full bit-exactness preserved for every other value in the operand's range -- exactly the narrow, value-specific corruption class this project's broad/randomized testbench coverage was built to catch, in contrast to a trigger that happened to survive a narrower test suite.
